definition.description: Build through a declared 5–10 metre submaximal linear approach, initiate braking before the marked brake zone, use multiple controlled deceleration contacts, stop inside the protected finish zone, own a balanced bilateral athletic stick for the declared hold, then reset by walking. One repetition contains one approach, one planned linear stop, one terminal stick, and no turn or reacceleration.

environment.surface: clear, level, dry, high-traction non-slip lane with a marked approach, braking zone, finish zone, and protected runoff
environment.space: one protected 15–30 metre lane with no cross traffic and a visible coach sightline to braking contacts and finish
inspection: surface traction, debris, weather, footwear, cones, lane separation, and runoff
declared approach, braking, finish, walk-back, and waiting locations
coach sightline, stop signal, and participant understanding
environment.changeRule: Changing approach distance, entry speed, braking-zone length, finish target, hold, surface, cue, dose, timing, symptoms, or substitute requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: pain-free easy jogging and controlled walking stop
safe protected lane and shared stop signal
session braking, impact, lower-body, technical-fatigue, logistics, and duration budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, giving way, slip, unsafe lane, repeated line overrun, hard reaching stop, knee/trunk collapse, imbalance, or communication conflict
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal approach distance, entry intensity, braking contact count, stop distance, dose, rest, recovery, readiness threshold, clinical clearance, or performance outcome

provenance.identityAuthority: The landing/braking foundations packet: the stable identity is a declared submaximal linear approach, early multi-step braking, balanced bilateral terminal stick, and reset without a cut or reacceleration.

anatomy.laterality: alternating braking contacts ending in a bilateral athletic stick; record meaningful side asymmetry rather than assigning athlete skill labels
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, establish readiness, or guarantee sport transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate practice for slowing a submaximal linear approach only when the exact lane, entry speed, finish target, and total braking budget fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Start slowing before the cone, take controlled steps, and stop balanced inside the zone.
secondaryCues: build only to the declared easy jog
lower smoothly through several steps instead of reaching for one hard stop
finish quiet and balanced with both feet controlled
walk back, recover, and report symptoms
expectedSensations: moderate front-thigh, hip, calf, and foot braking effort
high attention to slowing and balanced final stance
unexpectedSensations: pain, giving way, slip, hard heel strike, knee/trunk collapse, dizziness, inability to stop, or marked side difference
athleteSupport.painGuidance: Stop rather than forcing a brake or finish through pain, instability, slip, dizziness, or another concerning symptom; report it and follow facility escalation policy.
selfChecks: braking began before the marked zone
the final stance was balanced in the finish zone
no turn, cut, or reacceleration was added

observationChecklist: exact approach, brake zone, finish zone, declared entry speed, and no-turn boundary
penultimate and braking contacts, foot placement, posture, knee/trunk control, final balance, and side asymmetry
surface, symptoms, valid stops, rest, and cumulative braking exposure

faultCorrections.late_braking: shorten or slow the approach and restore braking before the marked zone
faultCorrections.reaching_or_hard_stop: reduce entry speed and rehearse several smaller braking contacts
faultCorrections.line_overrun: enlarge the finish zone or shorten the approach; do not chase speed
faultCorrections.collapse_or_imbalance: stop the effort, reduce demand only if control returns, otherwise select another reviewed task after revalidation

demonstrationPlan: show the protected approach, brake zone, finish zone, walk-back route, and stop signal
show a lower-speed valid repetition with early braking and a quiet bilateral finish
show invalid late braking, one hard reaching stop, line overrun, collapse, and an added turn
confirm the athlete can state the zone, finish, and stop signal before speed rises
groupManagement: use one athlete per protected lane and keep all waiting athletes behind the start
release an athlete only after the prior athlete clears the finish and walk-back route
record declared and actual approach context, valid stops, first fault, symptoms, rest, and total braking exposure
maintain coach sightline to approach, contacts, terminal stick, and stop signal
modificationDecisionTree: if pain, giving way, slip, dizziness, unsafe lane, or communication failure occurs, stop and escalate under facility policy
if braking begins late or the finish is overrun, shorten or slow the approach and revalidate the exact profile
if controlled multi-step braking and balanced stick cannot be restored, end this task and select a separately reviewed option after full revalidation
if cue, direction, turn, reacceleration, timing protocol, or maximum-intent demand changes, do not substitute automatically; rerun identity, selection, budgets, logistics, duration, and validation
doNotUseWhen: the intended task is a reactive cue, cut, turn, reacceleration, max-sprint deceleration, jump landing, or conditioning shuttle
surface, lane, symptoms, braking control, recovery, supervision, or communication is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved symptoms, slips, line overruns, collapse, imbalance, unsafe conditions, or a mismatch between the requested task and this exact submaximal linear brake-to-stick contract.
supportOperations.retentionPolicy: Persist the versioned definition and exact variant, declared and actual approach context, brake and finish zones, valid stops, first fault, symptoms, rest, total braking exposure, substitution, stop reason, and generator/rendering versions under facility policy.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to approach, speed, braking-zone length, finish, hold, surface, cue, dose, timing, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The consolidated source rows omit a complete exact approach, braking, finish, dose, load, fatigue, support, alternate, and review contract.

legacy.description: Use a declared submaximal straight approach, begin braking before the zone, take multiple controlled steps, stop inside the zone, hold a balanced bilateral athletic stance, and walk back to reset.
legacy.tempo: easy build; brake before zone; multiple controlled steps; two-second quiet stick; walk-back reset
legacy.loadNote: Bodyweight horizontal braking. Exact approach distance, entry speed, braking-zone length, finish, hold, rest, and total exposure are delivery-profile specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate submaximal linear braking-to-stick card with explicit lane, finish, no-turn, no-reacceleration, quality, and stop boundaries.
legacy.coachLanguage: Protect the lane and quality; start with an easy approach and count only controlled early-brake stops.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Slow before the cone, use several controlled steps, finish balanced, walk back, and report symptoms.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact declared approach, braking, finish, lane, surface, symptom, supervision, and recovery context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: pain-free easy jogging and controlled bilateral stop
protected high-traction lane, marked brake/finish zones, and runoff
can follow the stop signal and demonstrate a lower-speed controlled stop
session braking, impact, and technical-fatigue budgets fit
stopSigns: pain, giving way, slip, hard reaching stop, repeated line overrun, stumble, knee/trunk collapse, imbalance, unsafe lane, marked asymmetry, or participant stop request
fatigue that prevents early multi-step braking or a balanced bilateral finish
contraindications: symptom, unsafe surface/lane, inadequate braking control, recovery, supervision, or communication
reactive cue, cut, turn, reacceleration, maximal sprint-deceleration, jump, or testing protocol without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute reactive stops, cutting, turn-and-sprint, jump landing, or maximal-sprint deceleration work.

score.difficultyRationale: The score describes exercise complexity and physical difficulty for a declared submaximal brake-to-stick task, not participant ability, experience, age, or readiness. Early multi-step braking, momentum management, terminal balance, and impact raise complexity; speed and body mass remain delivery and workout inputs.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact submaximal linear approach, multi-step braking, bilateral terminal stick, and no turn or reacceleration.

variants.displayName: Submaximal Linear Multi-Step Deceleration to Bilateral Stick

programmingProfile.weeklyExposure: candidate_review_required; program from total braking exposure rather than a universal frequency
prerequisites: protected marked lane and understood stop signal
programmingProfile.completionCriteria: all repetitions satisfy the declared approach, early multi-step braking, finish-zone, terminal-stick, and stop-rule contract
programmingProfile.sequenceRules: Place after general preparation and before higher-speed sprint, change-of-direction, jump, or fatigue-heavy lower-body work when braking quality is the priority.
programmingProfile.pairingCompatibility: May pair only with low-fatigue mobility, simple trunk control, or noncompeting upper-body work when lane traffic, recovery, and total braking budget remain valid.
programmingProfile.interferenceRules: Do not stack with high-intent deceleration, cutting, high-impact jumps, exhaustive lower-body work, or testing when quality or recovery falls.
programmingProfile.uncertaintyPolicy: Scores, dose, recovery, and progression are candidate planning estimates; require human review and rerun validation after any change.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Rehearse early multi-step linear braking and a quiet terminal stick at a declared easy approach speed.
deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Brake before the zone, use multiple controlled contacts, stop inside the finish zone, hold the bilateral stick, and show no stop event.
stopRules: pain, instability, slip, unsafe lane, or participant request
late braking, line overrun, hard reaching stop, collapse, imbalance, or an added turn
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Declare the approach, zones, finish, and hold. Start below speed that challenges braking, observe every contact, and count only valid quiet stops.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Build to the easy jog. Slow before the zone with several steps, stop balanced inside the zone, hold, then walk back.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Task-specific rehearsal of submaximal linear braking and terminal stance control; no universal outcome is claimed.

logistics.station: one marked, protected lane with one athlete at a time
logistics.durationFormula: setup plus valid approaches, walk-backs, rest, restarts, recording, and lane reset

doseScaling.approach: shorten approach before reducing braking quality
doseScaling.volume: add only while every stop remains valid

supportPrompts.athlete: Slow before the cone; several quiet steps; finish balanced.
supportPrompts.coach: Early braking and a quiet finish count; speed does not.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Maintain a declared submaximal brake-to-stick task before later output work without turning it into maximal sprint deceleration.

dosage.intensity: declared 60-70 percent only if the movement-intelligence profile is already clean

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: All braking starts early, stays multi-step and controlled, ends in the zone with a balanced stick, and does not reduce quality for later work.
stopRules: quality decline, increased braking demand, or interference with subsequent planned output
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Use sparingly, preserve full recovery, and remove the profile rather than increasing speed if it compromises later output work.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Use the same early brake and balanced stick. Do not chase speed; save quality for the session.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate readiness rehearsal under a declared submaximal context; no performance transfer is asserted.

logistics.station: protected single-athlete lane with clear downstream output traffic separation
logistics.durationFormula: setup plus valid approaches, walk-backs, full recovery, recording, and transition

doseScaling.volume: do not add volume in this profile; remove before raising speed
doseScaling.speed: a speed increase requires revalidation and may belong to another exact profile

supportPrompts.athlete: Same quiet stop—do not race it.
supportPrompts.coach: Protect later output; remove this before quality drops.
